equipment.name: Treadmill
howToUse: Locate Stop and attach the safety clip to clothing if provided; test it as instructed by the manufacturer.
Mount using the fixed platforms and handrails according to the machine's placard; start the belt at its lowest walking speed.
Increase one setting gradually while keeping a natural gait. Slow down instead of hanging from the rails.
Reduce speed, stop the belt fully, and use the rails to step off. Never jump onto or off a moving belt.
equipment.notes: Controls vary by model; follow its placard and staff orientation.

equipment.name: Stair machine
howToUse: Find the stop control and use fixed steps and handrails to mount with the machine stopped, following its placard.
Face forward and place enough of each foot securely on the tread; keep shoes clear of moving edges.
Begin at the lowest pace and increase gradually. Stay upright with light rail contact rather than supporting bodyweight on the arms.
Slow and stop the steps fully before dismounting with the handrails. Record steps/min and floors from the console when available.
equipment.notes: Controls vary by model; follow its placard and staff orientation.

equipment.name: Exercise bike
howToUse: With the pedal farthest away, keep a small knee bend without rocking the hips. Adjust and lock the seat while stopped.
Set the seat and handlebar reach for relaxed shoulders. Secure shoes using the intended pedal straps; keep laces clear.
Start at low resistance and learn the model's braking controls. Fixed-gear pedals keep moving with the flywheel; use its brake before dismounting.
Select time and distance display units. Record resistance as the machine's setting; levels are not comparable across models.
equipment.notes: Controls vary by model; follow its placard and staff orientation.

equipment.name: Rowing machine
howToUse: Adjust the heel cups so the straps cross the widest part of the feet. Snug the straps without cutting circulation.
Check the seat slides smoothly and the rail is clear. Sit balanced with relaxed shoulders and a secure, light handle grip.
Start with an easy setting and learn the stroke. An air damper changes airflow and stroke feel; it is not a universal resistance or intensity scale.
Choose time and distance, normally meters, and begin with easy strokes. Park the handle safely and release the straps before standing.
equipment.notes: Controls vary by model; follow its placard and staff orientation.

exercises.name: Walking
setup: Choose a clear route with secure footing and suitable shoes.
For a treadmill, follow its setup guide, safety-stop instructions and gradual start procedure.
Begin easily and set a pace that lets you maintain a relaxed, controlled gait.
steps: Move forward with a tall, relaxed trunk and natural arm swing.
Use comfortable strides rather than reaching far ahead of the body.
Build pace or incline gradually; on a treadmill, keep position on the belt without holding your bodyweight on the rails.
Slow gradually at the end; stop a treadmill fully before stepping off.
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; reduce intensity if you cannot maintain control. Do not hold your breath through intervals.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Outdoor or bodyweight option; use the separate machine variation when training indoors.
safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Build total duration gradually before adding harder intervals.
Use an easy warm-up and cool-down, and reduce impact if joints become painful.
mistakes: Overstriding: shorten the stride and keep foot contacts controlled.
Increasing pace and incline abruptly: change one setting gradually.
Leaning on treadmill rails: reduce speed or incline until you can move with light balance support only.

exercises.name: Bicycling
setup: On a stationary bike, adjust and lock the seat so the knee remains slightly bent at the farthest pedal position.
Set a comfortable handlebar reach and secure feet using the intended pedals or straps.
Begin at easy resistance. Outdoors, use a suitable helmet, inspect the bicycle and follow local road rules.
steps: Pedal smoothly with knees tracking comfortably over the feet.
Keep the hips steady and the shoulders relaxed rather than gripping the bars tightly.
Adjust resistance gradually while maintaining controlled pedaling.
Ease the pace to finish; on a fixed-gear bike, use the brake and wait for the flywheel and pedals to stop before dismounting.
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; reduce intensity if you cannot maintain control. Do not hold your breath through intervals.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Outdoor or bodyweight option; use the separate machine variation when training indoors.
safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Recheck seat adjustment if knee or hip discomfort appears.
Learn the machine's braking behavior before attempting hard intervals.
mistakes: Rocking the hips: check seat height and reduce resistance.
Grinding against excessive resistance: lower the setting and restore smooth pedal motion.
Dismounting while fixed-gear pedals turn: brake and wait for a complete stop.

exercises.name: Rowing
setup: Adjust the footrests so the straps cross the widest part of each foot and secure them comfortably.
Check the seat and rail, take a light handle grip and choose an easy resistance or damper setting.
At the catch, reach with relaxed shoulders, a controlled hip hinge and shins close to vertical without forcing compression.
steps: Push with the legs first while keeping the arms long and the trunk supported.
As the legs extend, swing the torso slightly back from the hips, then draw the handle toward the lower ribs.
Recover in reverse order: arms away, hinge the torso forward, then bend the knees to slide forward.
Repeat smoothly without slamming the seat or yanking the chain; ease off before parking the handle.
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; reduce intensity if you cannot maintain control. Do not hold your breath through intervals.

equipmentSetup.position: Adjust the heel cups so the straps cross the widest part of the feet. Snug the straps without cutting circulation.
notes: Check the seat slides smoothly and the rail is clear. Sit balanced with relaxed shoulders and a secure, light handle grip.
Start with an easy setting and learn the stroke. An air damper changes airflow and stroke feel; it is not a universal resistance or intensity scale.
Choose time and distance, normally meters, and begin with easy strokes. Park the handle safely and release the straps before standing.

exercises.equipmentNotes: Use the linked machine setup guide.
safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Use slower practice strokes before increasing power or stroke rate.
Keep the grip light and stop if the back or wrists become painful.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms before driving the legs: restore the legs-body-arms sequence.
Rounding or throwing the lower back: shorten the reach and control the hip hinge.
Treating maximum damper as the best workout: learn technique at an easy setting; record the machine setting separately from effort.

exercises.name: Jumping jacks
setup: Use a clear, nonslip surface with overhead and side clearance.
Wear secure shoes and start with feet together, arms relaxed by the sides.
Choose small jumps or use alternating step-outs if a lower-impact option is needed.
steps: Make a small jump to move the feet apart while raising the arms comfortably out and up.
Land softly with knees tracking with the feet rather than collapsing inward.
Jump back to feet together as the arms return to the sides; this out-and-back cycle is one rep.
Repeat at a controllable rhythm, stopping the set if landing quality or balance deteriorates.
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; reduce intensity if you cannot maintain control. Do not hold your breath through intervals.
exercises.equipmentNotes: No equipment needed; use a clear, nonslip surface.
exercises.target: Quadriceps; Gastrocnemius (calf); Gluteus medius / minimus (hip stabilizers)
safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Build repetitions gradually and allow enough recovery between sets.
Use step jacks for less impact if jumping causes discomfort.
mistakes: Landing with stiff knees: soften the landing and reduce jump height.
Knees collapsing inward: slow down and keep knees aligned with the feet.
Forcing the arms overhead through pain: use a comfortable reach or a step-jack variation.

exercises.name: Climbing stairs
setup: Choose dry, clear stairs with a usable handrail, or follow the stair machine's setup guide.
Wear secure footwear and locate the machine stop control before starting.
Start at a slow pace that allows secure foot placement.
steps: Face forward and step onto each tread with controlled foot placement.
Push through the supporting leg while keeping the trunk upright.
Use the handrail for balance; reduce pace if you need to hang from it.
Slow before ending. Stop a machine fully before dismounting; descend real stairs carefully.
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; reduce intensity if you cannot maintain control. Do not hold your breath through intervals.
exercises.equipmentNotes: Outdoor or bodyweight option; use the separate machine variation when training indoors.
safetyTips: Warm up at an easy pace and build intensity gradually.
Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness or sharp pain. Get appropriate medical advice before vigorous intervals if you have symptoms or a relevant health condition.
injuryPrevention: Start with short bouts and increase time as balance and conditioning allow.
Use a secure handrail and keep clear of moving step edges.
mistakes: Skipping treads at an uncontrolled pace: return to single, secure steps.
Supporting bodyweight on the rails: lower speed and restore upright posture.
Turning around on moving steps: remain forward-facing and stop before dismounting.
